m: b. Wāqid, from al-Rabīʿ b. Anas, from Abū l-ʿĀliya, who said: Ubayy b. Kaʿb related to me, he said: There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection. x: The correct view on this in our opinion is to say:
h
kuwwirat

, as God, Mighty is His praise, said. Takwīr in the speech of the Arabs is gathering one part of a thing to another, such as the winding of the turban, which is its coiling around the head, and such as the bundling of the kāra, which is gathering garments together and folding them up. So too His saying:
h
When the sun is wrapped up

: its meaning is only that its parts are gathered together, then it is rolled up and cast away; and when that is done to it, its light goes away. Thus, according to the interpretation we have adopted and explained, each of the two views I have mentioned from the interpreters has a sound basis, because when it is wrapped up and cast away, its light goes away.

c: Al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī al-Ṣudāʾī told us, he said: My father told us, from al-Fuḍayl, from ʿAṭiyya:
m: And by the night when it ʿasʿasa (17)
. He said: He pointed with his hand to the west (2).

x: The sounder of the two interpretations on this, in my view, is the view of those who said: The meaning of that is: when it departs; and that is because of His saying:
h
And by the dawn when it breathes (18)

. That indicates that the oath is by the night as it goes away and by the day as it comes on. The Arabs say: ʿasʿasa l-laylu and saʿsaʿa l-laylu, when it departs and only a little of it remains. From this is the saying of Ruʾba b. al-ʿAjjāj
n
O Hind, how quickly he has faded away (tasaʿsaʿa)!
Had he hoped to follow youth, he would have followed it That is the usage of those who say saʿsaʿa. As for the usage of those who say ʿasʿasa, there is the saying of ʿAlqama b. Qurṭ
n
Until, when the morning breathed for her
n
and her night was drawn off from her and ʿasʿasa
meaning: it departed. Some of those with knowledge of the speech of the Arabs used to claim that ʿasʿasa means: it drew near at its beginning and grew dark. Al-Farrāʾ said
n
: Abū l-Bilād the grammarian
n
used to recite a verse:
ʿAsʿasa until, had he wished to draw near (iddanā),
he would have had a firebrand from its light
He intends: had he wished, when he drew near (idh danā); but he assimilated the dhāl into the dāl. Al-Farrāʾ said: They used to think that this verse was fabricated.

evidence.text: Muḥammad b. Yazīd told us, from Ismāʿīl b. Abī Khālid, from a man, from Abū Ẓabyān, he said: I was following ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, may God be pleased with him, as he was going out toward the east; he faced the dawn and recited this verse: {And by the night when it ʿasʿasa} (4).

x: His saying:
h
And by the dawn when it breathes (18)
. He says: and by the light of day when it comes on and becomes clear.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yamān told us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd
m: And by the dawn when it breathes (18)

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: And by the dawn when it breathes (18)
: when it lights up and comes on

x: His saying: it is
h
Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger (19)
. The Exalted says: this Qur'an is the revelation of
h
a noble messenger
. He means Gabriel, who sent it down to Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger (19)

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:

x: His saying:
h
Possessed of power, secure in position with the Possessor of the Throne (20)
. The Exalted says:
h
Possessed of power
. He means Gabriel, in whatever matter he is charged with, not incapable of it
n
h
secure in position with the Possessor of the Throne
. He says: he is of high standing with the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Obeyed there, and trustworthy (21) And your companion is not mad (22) And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon (23) And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy (ḍanīn) (4) (24) And it is not the word of an accursed devil (25) So where are you going? (26)
The Exalted says:
h
Obeyed there
. He means Gabriel, peace be upon him,
h
obeyed
in heaven; the angels obey him; he is
h
trustworthy
. He says: trustworthy with God over His revelation and His message, and other things with which He has entrusted him.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū l-Sāʾib told me, he said:
m: told us, from Ismāʿīl b. Abī Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ:
. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, trusted to enter seventy pavilions of light without permission

c: Muḥammad b. Manṣūr al-Ṭūsī told us, he said: ʿUmar b. Shabīb told us, he said: Ismāʿīl b. Abī Khālid told us, he said:
m: I know it only from Abū Ṣāliḥ, the like of it.

c: Sulaymān b. ʿUmar b. Khālid al-Aqṭaʿ told us, he said: My father ʿUmar b. Khālid related to me, from Maʿqil b.
m: ʿUbayd Allāh al-Jazarī, he said: Maymūn b. Mihrān said regarding His saying:
. He said: That is Gabriel, peace be upon him

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: Possessed of power, secure in position with the Possessor of the Throne (20) Obeyed there, and trustworthy (21)

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: Possessed of power] (2) with the Possessor of the Throne, secure in position (20) Obeyed

x: I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
: he means Gabriel, peace be upon him (1).

x: His saying:
h
And your companion is not mad (22)

. The Exalted says: and your companion, O people — Muḥammad — is not mad, such that he would speak out of madness and rave as the mad rave; rather, he has come with the truth and confirmed the messengers.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:
Sulaymān b. ʿUmar b. Khālid al-Raqqī
n
told us, he said: My father ʿUmar
n
b. Khālid told us, from Maʿqil b. ʿUbayd
n
Allāh al-Jazarī, he said: Maymūn b. Mihrān said:
h
And your companion is not mad (22)
. He said: That is Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace
n
His saying:
h
And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon

. The Exalted says: and Muḥammad certainly saw Gabriel, may God bless them both and grant them peace, in his form, in the quarter that makes things clear, so that they are seen from it; and that is from the direction of the rising of the sun, from the east.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
: the highest. He said: On a horizon in the direction of Ajyād

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: . He said: We used to be told that the horizon is where the sun rises

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon
: We used to be told that it is the horizon from which the day comes.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon
. He said: He saw Gabriel on the clear horizon

c: ʿĪsā b. ʿUthmān b. ʿĪsā al-Ramlī told me, he said: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā told us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Walīd b.
m: al-ʿAyzār, he said: I heard Abū l-Aḥwaṣ say regarding God's saying:
And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon
. He said: He saw Gabriel, who has six hundred wings, in his own form

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿĀmir, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his own form only once; he used to come to him in the form of a man called Diḥya. On the day he saw him in his own form, he came to him having blocked the whole horizon, wearing green brocade hung with pearls; that is God's saying:
And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon (23)

x: It is mentioned that this passage in
h
When the sun is wrapped up (1)
h
Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger (19)
is about Gabriel, up to His saying:
h
And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy (24)
, which means the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
His saying:
h
And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy (biḍanīn)
n
. The reciters differed over the reading of that. The general body of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it:
h
biḍanīn
with ḍād
n
, meaning that he is not miserly toward them in teaching them what God taught him and sent down to him of His Book.
Some of the Meccans, some of the Basrans and some of the Kufans read it: (biẓanīn)
n
with ẓāʾ, meaning that he is not suspected regarding the reports he gives them from God.
Mention of those among the interpreters who read
n
it with ḍād and interpreted it in the way we have described:

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr:
m: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn). He said: The ẓanīn is the suspected one. And in your reading,
: the ḍanīn is the miser; and the unseen is the Qur'an

c: Bishr told us, he said: Khālid b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Wāsiṭī told us, he said: Mughīra told us, from Ibrāhīm:
m: And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy
. He said: He does not withhold from you what he knows

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy

. He said: This Qur'an is unseen; God gave it to Muḥammad, and he gave it out freely, taught it and called to it; by God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not withhold it

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr:
m: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn). He said: In our reading: "suspected"; and whoever reads it
And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy

: The unseen is the Qur'an; he did not withhold it from anyone among the people; he delivered it and conveyed it. God sent with it the Trustworthy Spirit, Gabriel, to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace; Gabriel delivered what God had entrusted to him to Muḥammad, and Muḥammad delivered what God and Gabriel had entrusted to him to the servants; none of them withheld, concealed, or invented falsehood

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿĀmir:
m: And he is not, concerning the unseen, stingy
: God: he means the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Mention of those who said it with ẓāʾ and interpreted it as we have mentioned, among the interpreters:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: al-Muḥāribī told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: that he read: (biẓanīn). He said: Not suspected

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Abū l-Muʿallā, from Saʿīd b.
m: Jubayr, that he used to read this word: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn). I said to Saʿīd b. Jubayr: What is the ẓanīn? He said: Not suspected

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abū l-Muʿallā, from Saʿīd b.
m: Jubayr that he read: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn). I said: And what is the ẓanīn? He said: The suspected.

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: regarding His saying: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn). He says: He is not suspected regarding what he has brought, and what he has been given is not doubted

c: Bishr told us, he said: Khālid b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Wāsiṭī told us, he said: al-Mughīra told us, from Ibrāhīm:
m: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn). He said: Suspected

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr:
m: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn). He said: The unseen is the Qur'an; and in our reading: (biẓanīn): suspected (2).

x: I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying: (biẓanīn). He said: He is not suspected regarding what God sent down

x: Some of the people of Arabic
n
have also interpreted that to mean: and he is not weak concerning the unseen, but is able to bear it and capable of it. He took it in the sense of the Arabs' saying of a weak man: he is ẓanūn.
The sounder of the two readings on this, in my view, is that on which the written forms of the Muslims' codices agree, even if their readings of it differ, and that is:
h
biḍanīn
with ḍād
n

; because it is all written thus in their writing. Since that is so, the sounder of the two interpretations is the interpretation of those who interpreted it as: and Muḥammad is not miserly, regarding what God taught him of His revelation and what He sent down, in teaching it to you, O people; rather he is eager that you believe in it and learn it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed over the reading of that.
The general body of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it: {biḍanīn} with ḍād (3), meaning that he is not miserly toward them in teaching them what God taught him and sent down to him of His Book.
Some of the Meccans, some of the Basrans and some of the Kufans read it: (biẓanīn) (4) with ẓāʾ, meaning that he is not suspected regarding the reports he gives them from God.
He said: In our reading: "suspected"; and whoever reads it {biḍanīn} means: "miserly" (1).
Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Abū l-Muʿallā, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, that he used to read this word: (wa-mā huwa ʿalā l-ghaybi biẓanīn).
He said: The unseen is the Qur'an; and in our reading: (biẓanīn): suspected (2).

The sounder of the two readings on this, in my view, is that on which the written forms of the Muslims' codices agree, even if their readings of it differ, and that is: {biḍanīn} with ḍād (5); because it is all written thus in their writing.

x: His saying:
h
And it is not the word of an accursed devil
. The Exalted says: this Qur'an is not the word of a cursed, banished devil, but it is the speech of God and His revelation.
His saying:
h
So where are you going?
The Exalted says: so where are you going, away from this Qur'an, and turning aside from it?
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: : He says: so where are you turning aside from my Book and obedience to me?

x: It was said:
h
fa-ayna tadhhabūn
and not "fa-ilā ayna tadhhabūn", as one says: I went (to) Syria, and I went (to) the market. And it is reported, as heard from the Arabs: "he was taken off (to) the immediate [place]"
n
, in the sense of dropping
n
the particle. A verse is also recited of one of Banū ʿUqayl
n
Ḥanīfa shouts at us when she sees us,
and to what land do you go to shout?
meaning: to what land (ilā ayyi l-arḍi) do you go? Dropping the particle in this is permitted on account of usage.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
It is not but a reminder to the worlds (27) For whoever among you wills to take a straight course (28) And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds (29)
The Exalted says: this Qur'an — and His saying
h
huwa
refers to the mention of the Qur'an — is
h
not but a reminder to the worlds
. He says: only an admonition and exhortation for the worlds, of jinn and humankind,
h
for whoever among you wills to take a straight course
. So the Exalted made it a reminder for those among the worlds who will to take a straight course, and did not make it a reminder for all of them. The lām in His saying
h
for whoever among you wills
is a substitution (badal) for the lām in
h
to the worlds
. It is as if the meaning of the sentence were: it is only a reminder for whoever among you wills to be upright on the path of truth, so that he follows it and believes in it.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
for whoever among you wills to take a straight course
. He said: To follow the truth

x: His saying:
h
And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds
. The Exalted says: and you do not will, O people, uprightness on the truth, unless God wills that for you.
It is mentioned that the occasion on which this verse was revealed is what Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said:

c: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Saʿīd b.
m: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Sulaymān, he said: When
for whoever among you wills to take a straight course
was revealed, Abū Jahl said: That is up to us; if we wish, we will be upright. So
And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds (29)

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Saʿīd b.
m: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Sulaymān b. Mūsā, he said: When this verse was revealed:
for whoever among you wills to take a straight course
, Abū Jahl said: The matter is up to us; if we wish we will be upright, and if we wish we will not be upright. So God revealed:
And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds

c: Ibn al-Barqī told me, he said: ʿAmr b. Abī Salama told us, from Saʿīd, from Sulaymān b.
m: Mūsā, he said: When this verse was revealed:
for whoever among you wills to take a straight course
, Abū Jahl said: That is up to us; if we wish we will be upright, and if we wish we will not be upright. So God revealed:
And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds

x: End of the commentary on the sura "When the sun is wrapped up".
